```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day paying-customer goal hinges on sales-cycle length. Idea B's own seed source (dashp) reports about 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal, which alone overshoots the 90-day window. Idea A sells through the Shopify App Store, a self-serve marketplace where a merchant can install and pay without any sales conversation.",
    "Idea A's channel suits one person running AI agents. App Store listings, CPC ads (about $6 per click) and SEO comparison content can be produced and run without the founder being physically present. Idea B's channels are office visits, referrals and a trade show whose 2026 booths are already sold out, and the brief itself flags that AI agents don't obviously remove the trust bottleneck.",
    "Idea A has a larger contestable market. Its six-plus competitors with free tiers squeeze pricing, but each represents a mature, wide merchant base. Idea B's founder source puts its total market at only 'hundreds' of companies and calls it unsuited to performance marketing, with 8 competitors identified, including a second solo builder running the same playbook today.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence comes from the payer. The Reddit quote is from a Shopify merchant, the person who would buy, describing the exact pain and saying manual workarounds failed. Idea B's demand quotes come from reps and litigants, not from the owners who would pay.",
    "Idea A carries lighter regulatory exposure for a solo operator. A one-time DPA and privacy review is a contained cost, while Idea B adds open-ended state wage-law and 1099 commission-calculation liability."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence does not come from the buyer. One quote is a pest control technician's complaint on a consumer-complaints site about a single employer's unpaid commissions. The other is a litigated commission dispute over $217K. Both show reps suffer from commission errors, but neither shows that pest control owners, the stated payer, want or would pay for tracking software. If anything, the lawsuit suggests some owners benefit from opacity.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Idea A is far from strong. Its demand evidence is a single Reddit post, its category success story (Zigpoll) took two years to reach traction, and competitors' free tiers may keep a zero-review app from converting installs to paid within 90 days. The decision rests mainly on Idea B's documented 5-month sales cycle and tiny market, which directly conflict with the 90-day goal. Idea A's problems are risks that a market test could resolve, not structural blockers."
}
```
